justification:
CVE-2025-41110 affected the Ghost Robotics Vision 60 robot, where encrypted WiFi and SSH credentials were discovered embedded in the Android APK (v0.27.2). An attacker who decompiled the APK could extract these credentials to join the robot's WiFi network, view all traffic, and gain full SSH control over the device. Because the robot runs ROS 2 without default authentication, this gave the attacker the ability to inflict physical damage to the robot or its surroundings (CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials, CVSS 8.8 HIGH).

The synthetic vulnerability in Home Assistant Android replicates this same weakness class: the patch adds hardcoded admin credentials (username and password) as constants in AuthenticationService.kt's companion object, alongside existing constants like CLIENT_ID. These credentials correspond to a pre-seeded admin account on the Home Assistant server. An attacker who decompiles the APK can extract these credentials and use the Home Assistant REST API login flow to authenticate as the admin user, gaining full control over the smart home instance — including the ability to control IoT devices (lights, locks, thermostats, alarms), read sensor data, and modify automations.

Both CVE-2025-41110 and this synthetic vulnerability share the same fundamental flaw: a mobile application ships with privileged credentials embedded in its package, allowing an attacker with access to the APK to authenticate to the backend system without any prior knowledge. In both cases, the compromised access enables control over physical-world systems (a robot in the original CVE, smart home devices in the synthetic). The attack vector (adjacent network), complexity (low), and impact profile (high confidentiality, integrity, and availability) are identical.
